newsitem.title: GERMANY: German PR agencies post 1996 turnover growth.
newsitem.headline: German PR agencies post 1996 turnover growth.

text.p: The main German public relations association, the GPRA, said on Thursday most of its members had posted growth in turnover for 1996 and expected further boosts in fee income for the current year.

The total fee turnover of 35 of the 41 GPRA agencies climbed seven percent in 1996 to about 200 million marks ($116 million), the GPRA said. The number of employees increased at the same rate to 1,088.

"There has been an increasing demand for coordination of communications work, and for consultation in the various communications fields," GPRA president Dietmar Mueller said. "This is also true for medium-sized companies."

Duesseldorf-based public relations agency Kothes & Klewes Kommunication GmbH topped the ranks in turnover among GPRA members, the association said, posting fee income of 28.4 million marks for 1996, 18 percent above its 1995 turnover.

In second place, communications consultants Euro-RSCG group reported 27.7 million marks in turnover. The GPRA listed Frankfurt-based agency Leipziger & Partner Kommunikations GmbH as the third largest, with 21.1 million marks in fee income.

The GPRA said only 28 of the agencies it represents had had their results checked by a tax adviser or an accountant, as the association requires. The remaining agencies will present auditors' reports by the end of June, the GPRA said.

The association did not report the size of the German public relations market share it represents. Industry sources estimate the number of public relations agencies in Germany at about 800. ($ = 1.727 German Marks)
